# Intake Brief: Park should give a good reputation bonus

**Work item:** MS-0MVRDGNFU001DDQW · `feature` · `medium`
**Status:** Producer answers recorded (2026-10-28): **+20 reputation/turn, pricing maintained (150 / 40)** — ready for planning.

## Headline

The Park (`cs-park`) is the **only community space that yields no reputation per
turn**, while carrying the **highest running cost in the game** (40 coins/turn)
— it produces neither income nor reputation and the balance analysis records it
as a net drain. Give it the producer-confirmed **+20 reputation/turn**, keeping
its cost 150 and 40/turn running cost unchanged, restoring it as an attractive
tier-1 Entertainment anchor and the cheapest reputation entry in the game.

## Problem statement

The Park currently provides no value to the player. All seven other community
spaces generate `reputationPerTurn` (Playground 20, Garden 40, Fountain 40,
Library 40, Health Kiosk 60, Shelter 60, Public Art 80); the Park has an empty
`reputationPerTurn` (0) while costing 40 coins/turn to run — the highest
`ongoingCost` of any community space. `docs/dev/analysis/community-space-event-repricing.md`
records it as a "pure net drain" (remedied by re-pricing 300 → 150 in
MS-0MUR9IN7L0004TO5, but the zero reputation remained). The producer decision
(2026-10-28) sets **+20 reputation/turn** with pricing kept at 150/40.

## Users

- **Player** — building an Entertainment cluster should feel rewarded: the Park
  is a tier-1, tutorial-visible card that currently reads as a money pit.
  *"As a player, I want the Park to grow my reputation, so that placing it is a
  strategic choice rather than an obvious mistake."*
- **Producer / balance owner** — confirmed the value and pricing on
  2026-10-28; wants the guardrails verified and the docs updated to match.
- **Developer** — a single-row, data-only change: the machinery that applies
  `reputationPerTurn` (per-turn income, tooltips, AI scoring) already exists and
  needs no engine changes.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Card data** — `cs-park` in `src/card-data.csv` gains `reputationPerTurn = 20`
   (producer-confirmed 2026-10-28; integer, no cost or `ongoingCost` change —
   remains 150 and 40). The description is updated with the existing wording
   convention used by Library/Garden/Fountain ("Provides +20 reputation per
   turn."), and the `card-text-data-consistency` test passes.
2. **Value visible automatically** — the Park's card tooltip shows the +20
   rep/turn line, the per-turn reputation total includes it (existing
   `MainStreetEngineCommands` path), and UI/AI scoring that reads
   `reputationPerTurn` reflect the new value with no engine change.
3. **Retune-contract baseline updated deliberately** —
   `tests/main-street/reputation-retune-contract.test.ts` pins `cs-park: 0`
   (`PRE_RETUNE_COMMUNITY_SPACE_REP`). This is the only card whose value
   changes outside the ×4 retune (MS-0MUR9IMN60093HIE), so the baseline entry
   and the test's rationale comment are updated with a pointer to this item
   (a deliberate, documented contract change, not a silent regression).
4. **Balance sanity** — the Monte Carlo / tutorial guardrails remain within
   band after the change (Park now contributes +20 passive reputation and looks
   more attractive to the AI's community-space scoring); any drift is measured
   and reported, and no band is silently widened.
5. **Documentation updated** — `docs/game/card-catalog.md` (Park row and its
   rationale line about "zero reputation and negative net value"),
   `docs/game/content-design-and-progression.md` (community-space table), and
   any other doc listing Park's rep/turn (e.g.
   `docs/dev/analysis/community-space-event-repricing.md` note) are updated to
   the confirmed +20 value.
6. **Regeneration** — CSV-derived static SVGs/checksum
   (`public/assets/games/main-street/svg/cards/csv-checksum.json`) are
   regenerated; card face text reflects the new description.
7. **Full project test suite passes with the new changes** (including any
   existing tests that assert Park has no reputation, e.g.
   `tests/main-street/card-diagrams.test.ts` Park detail).

## Constraints

- **Integer economy (hard):** reputation per turn must be a whole number (20).
- **Balance levers only:** changes are limited to `card-data.csv`
   (`reputationPerTurn`) and description/docs; **no cost/ongoingCost change**
   (producer decision Q2 = maintain 150 / 40) and no engine-rule changes.
   Values are data-is-source-of-truth.
- **Do not break the win-rate ladder** `Easy ≥ Medium ≥ Hard` (primary balance
   gate).
- **No new cards, no scope creep:** `upg-garden` (Park → Garden upgrade),
   other card values, and AI heuristic changes are out of scope.

## Existing state

- `src/card-data.csv` `cs-park`: cost **150**, `baseIncome` 0, Entertainment,
  `ongoingCost` **40**, `reputationPerTurn` empty (0). Description: "Offers
  leisure space. Gains {SYNERGY_RATE} of base income per adjacent Entertainment
  business or community space. Costs 40 coins per turn to run."
- Current community-space reputation set (post-×4 retune,
  MS-0MUR9IMN60093HIE): Playground 20 (300/ongoing 20), Garden 40 (350/10),
  Fountain 40 (350/25), Library 40 (400/25), Health Kiosk 60 (450/15),
  Shelter 60 (400/30), Public Art 80 (600/25). Park is the outlier at 0.
- Confirmed target (+20 rep, 150/40): rep per 100 coins of cost = 13.3 — inside
  the community-space band (Playground 6.7 … Shelter 15; Public Art/Kiosk 13.3),
  and still net-negative in coin-equivalent (−10 coins/turn at the documented
  1.5 coins/rep) — a deliberate producer choice: the Park is a cheap
  reputation-first card with the game's highest upkeep, not a coin earner.
- Test contracts that pin current Park values:
  `tests/main-street/reputation-retune-contract.test.ts:66` (`'cs-park': 0`),
  `tests/main-street/community-space-tooltip.test.ts` (Park tooltip),
  `tests/main-street/cash-line-overlay.test.ts:259`, `card-diagrams.test.ts`
  (Park detail), `community-space-ongoing-cost.test.ts` (Park fixtures).

## Desired change

1. Set `cs-park.reputationPerTurn = 20` in `src/card-data.csv` and update the
   card description to state "Provides +20 reputation per turn." in the
   existing wording convention.
2. Keep `cost` 150 and `ongoingCost` 40 (producer decision Q2).
3. Update the docs tables and the retune-contract test baseline (deliberate
   change), and regenerate the CSV-derived card artefacts.

**Key Files:**

- `src/card-data.csv` — `cs-park` row: `reputationPerTurn` + description text.
- `tests/main-street/reputation-retune-contract.test.ts` — `'cs-park': 0`
  baseline + rationale comment (deliberate contract change).
- `tests/main-street/card-text-data-consistency.test.ts` — enforces
  data/description agreement for the "+20 reputation per turn" wording.
- `tests/main-street/card-diagrams.test.ts` — Park diagram detail test.
- `tests/main-street/community-space-tooltip.test.ts` — Park tooltip assertion.
- `tests/main-street/community-space-ai-scoring.test.ts` —
  Park fixtures/expectations may shift as AI now scores its reputation.
- `tests/main-street/cash-line-overlay.test.ts` — Park cash-line fixture.
- `tests/main-street/community-space-ongoing-cost.test.ts` — Park
  ongoing-cost fixtures.
- `tests/main-street/monte-carlo-greedy-guardrail.test.ts` — balance gate
  evidencing the change (drift measured, not silently widened).
- `src/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs` — regenerates the
  CSV-derived SVG/checksum artefacts.
- `public/assets/games/main-street/svg/cards/csv-checksum.json` — regenerated.
- `docs/game/card-catalog.md` — Park row and its rationale line.
- `docs/game/content-design-and-progression.md` — community-space table.
- `docs/dev/analysis/community-space-event-repricing.md` — repricing note.

## Related work

- **MS-0MUR9IMN60093HIE** — Re-tune reputation sources (×4 retune) — left
  Park at 0 deliberately; the contract test that must be updated lives here.
- **MS-0MUR9IN7L0004TO5** — Re-price community spaces — set Park cost 150
  "to reflect its zero reputation and negative net value"; this item removes
  that premise.
- **MS-0MUMC6IVF0098WRL** — Per-turn running costs for Playground/Fountain/
  Shelter — established the producer-owned-value AC pattern and the
  description wording "Provides +N reputation per turn."
- **CG-0MU9NW9EP003B1AK** — Park 40/turn running cost (precedent).
- **CG-0MRXYGM9B006I3PE / CG-0MSKS963N000ZSTU** — Park-model synergy
  participation (unchanged by this item).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** no engine change is required — `reputationPerTurn` already
  flows into per-turn reputation (`MainStreetEngineCommands`), tooltips,
  diagram detail and AI scoring, all derived from CSV. Verified by source scan.
- **Balance drift:** giving Park +20 reputation changes AI placement desirability
  and the passive-reputation economy; run the guardrails and report drift
  rather than widening bands (per the drift-report-then-ask workflow).
- **Value-by-design:** at +20 the Park stays net-negative in coin-equivalent
  (−10/turn) — the producer's deliberate choice of a reputation-first card with
  the highest upkeep; the AC4 balance gate confirms the ladder is unaffected.
- **Contract-test coupling:** the ×4-retune contract deliberately pins
  `cs-park: 0`; updating it is expected but must be deliberate and documented
  (AC3), otherwise a reviewer will read it as a regression.
- **Scope creep:** upgrade-card economics (`upg-garden`), AI heuristics, and
  the other seven community spaces are out of scope; record as linked items.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: What reputation-per-turn should the Park provide? — **Answer (producer,
  2026-10-28): +20.** The intake recommendation was +40 (parity with
  Library/Garden/Fountain; the first value making the Park net-positive in
  coin-equivalent), and the producer chose the lower +20 instead. Accepted
  value: 20. Rationale the +20 choice is coherent: 20/150 cost gives 13.3 rep
  per 100 coins — inside the community-space band (Playground 6.7, Library 10,
  Kiosk/Public Art 13.3) — and the Park stays a cheap, reputation-first tier-1
  card whose high 40/turn upkeep is its built-in anti-spam lever. Source:
  interactive producer reply; evidence: `src/card-data.csv` community-space
  rows, `docs/dev/analysis/community-space-event-repricing.md`, MS-0MUR9IMN60093HIE,
  MS-0MUR9IN7L0004TO5.
- Q2: Keep cost 150 / ongoing 40, or re-price? — **Answer (producer,
  2026-10-28): maintain 150 / 40.** Accepted: pricing unchanged; only the
  `reputationPerTurn` value changes in AC1. Preserves the MS-0MUR9IN7L0004TO5
  repricing intent and the CG-0MU9NW9EP003B1AK running-cost precedent.
- Q3 (answered, agent): Description wording? — Use the shipped convention
  ("Provides +N reputation per turn.") matching Library/Garden/Fountain, since
  `card-text-data-consistency.test.ts` enforces data/text agreement. Source:
  existing `card-data.csv` descriptions.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MV8LHN0W0017XU1** – Reputation bonuses should have no delay between businesses (completed)
- **MS-0MTV9AS15004AC1E** – Visual representation of reputation (completed)
- **MS-0MV8LHN5U008B9JJ** – AI staff should not give players bonuses (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/dev/analysis/community-space-event-repricing.md` — matched: bonus, currently, give, good, park (+6 more)
- `core/docs/the-build/concept-evaluation.md` — matched: bonus, give, good, park, player (+5 more)
- `docs/dev/prd-balance-process-and-tooling.md` — matched: bonus, currently, give, good, player (+5 more)

## Plan: changelog

- **2026-10-29 — plan (auto-complete path, effort Small / risk Medium).**
  Leaf `feature` with measurable ACs, a minimal implementation sketch, and
  producer answers already recorded at intake (Q1 +20 rep/turn, Q2 maintain
  150/40) — no decomposition needed and no child work items created. The item
  is a single small vertical slice spanning data, tests, docs and artefact
  regeneration; phasing was considered and rejected because every AC verifies
  the same one-row change.

  Six automated review stages ran against the existing content:
  - **Requirements & AC alignment** — all 7 ACs trace to the brief's
    requirements; AC1 reflects the producer's +20 and unchanged 150/40; no
    invented or contradictory criteria.
  - **Completeness** — normalised the Key Files heading to the machine-readable
    `**Key Files:**` form, split the combined docs bullet into one path per
    bullet, and added the missing verification files
    (`card-text-data-consistency.test.ts`, `cash-line-overlay.test.ts`,
    `community-space-ongoing-cost.test.ts`) plus the SVG generation script. All
    listed paths verified to exist.
  - **Sequencing & dependencies** — no children, so no dependency edges; the AC
    order follows test-first verification (contract baseline → data → docs →
    artefacts → full suite).
  - **Scope sizing** — single Small vertical slice; no phasing.
  - **Acceptance & testability** — every AC is pass/fail and testable.
  - **Polish & handoff** — description is actionable and copy-pasteable; this
    changelog records the handoff rationale.

  AC coverage review: `proceed` (leaf item; 7 ACs parsed; no children
  required). Effort/risk already computed at intake (Small / Medium, report
  MS-C0MVSNAEOV001X1FI); planning did not change scope, so no re-estimation.

### Appendix revision notes

- No new planning questions were asked: all planning inputs were resolved at
  intake (Q1–Q3 recorded in the Appendix above). Prior answers stand; no OPEN
  QUESTION remains.

## AC6 clarification (2026-11-03)

AC6's "card face text reflects the new description" refers to the **runtime** card face, not the pre-generated static SVG asset. The static CSV-derived faces (`public/assets/games/main-street/svg/cards/*.svg`) are name/cost/synergy only by design — they never bake the description or ongoing cost — so the description and per-turn reputation reach the card face through `src/scenes/MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` (`generateBusinessCardSvg`), which renders the Park's `+20/turn` reputation line from the CSV. This is pinned by `tests/main-street/park-reputation-bonus.test.ts` ("AC6: the runtime card face renders the +20 reputation line"). The static artefacts are regenerated and consistent: `public/assets/games/main-street/svg/cards/csv-checksum.json` matches the CSV (DJB2 `3c317c77`), and the card diagram (`docs/dev/assets/community-space-relationships.mmd`) shows `ongoing 40 coins/turn · +20 rep/turn`.

# Bank loan offer: show the shortfall needed to reach the next turn

## Problem statement

The bankruptcy bailout dialog (titled **Bank Loan Offer**) tells a player only
*"You cannot cover this turn's costs."* It never names the amount, so the player
cannot see how far short they are, cannot judge whether any offered loan is big
enough, and — in the case where even the largest option leaves them negative —
gets no warning at all before committing to debt that will not save the run.

## Users

- **Human player facing bankruptcy (single- and competitive mode)** — "When the
  Bank Loan Offer appears I want it to say how much cash I am short, so I know
  what has to be borrowed to reach the next turn."
- **Cost-conscious player** — "I want each loan option to tell me whether it
  actually covers the gap, so I do not borrow €300 when I am €800 short — or
  borrow more than I need because I had to do the arithmetic myself."
- **Player reading back the activity log** — "I want the bailout log row to state
  the shortfall in coins, not a raw negative balance I have to interpret."

Not a user of this item: AI/headless seats (they auto-accept the largest option
and never see the dialog) and mid-game borrowers (the Turn Summary loan selector,
MS-0MVPWSQMG004198C — see Non-goals).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **The offer states the amount.** While a bankruptcy bailout offer is open, the
   dialog states the exact amount of coins needed to reach the next turn, in the
   game's currency formatting (e.g. *"You are €80 short of covering this turn's
   costs."*), in place of the current amount-free sentence.
2. **The amount is the closing deficit.** The stated figure is the shortfall that
   triggered the offer: `max(0, −coins)` evaluated on the same balance the
   bankruptcy test used — the shared wallet in single-player, the seat's
   `PlayerRecord.coins` in competitive mode, and the **projected** closing balance
   on the deferred-mutation path — never a fresh re-read at render time. It
   excludes the loan's first instalment, which is charged on the next turn
   (docs §5.1, "First instalment timing"), and is a whole, non-negative coin
   amount.
3. **Per-option coverage.** Every option row states whether that loan closes the
   gap: rows that do state it closes the gap, and rows that do not state how many
   coins the seat would still be short after taking it (e.g. *"[ Borrow €300 —
   €110/turn, €330 total over 3 turns — €20 short ]"*). When **no** presented
   option closes the gap, the dialog additionally warns that any of these loans
   still leaves the seat below zero and the run will end.
4. **Log row agrees.** The activity-log row written when the offer is raised
   states the shortfall in coins (replacing the raw `coins are -80` phrasing) so
   the log and the dialog cannot disagree.
5. **Persistence.** The shortfall travels with the pending offer across a
   save/load round-trip, so a save taken mid-offer restores the same figure. A
   v3 (or v2) save whose pending offer carries no shortfall loads and behaves
   exactly as today — the offer is still resolvable and the figure is shown as
   unknown rather than being invented. **No save schema version bump** is
   required (the field is additive and optional inside the existing
   `pendingLoanOffer`).
6. **No behaviour change.** Offer-raising rules, the one-offer-per-seat-per-turn
   guard, the AI/headless largest-option policy, the loan menu, the repayment
   maths and the bankruptcy outcome are all unchanged; loans-off headless
   closings remain byte-identical (golden baseline still passes).
7. **Testing/validation.** Unit tests cover the shortfall computation
   (single-player, competitive seat, deferred projected balance, and the
   guard that a non-negative balance never raises an offer), the dialog model
   (intro text, per-row coverage flags, the no-option-covers warning, the
   back-compatible unknown-shortfall path), the save/load round-trip, and the
   rendered dialog text in the browser overlay suite.
8. **Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the
   changes, including code comments, `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md`
   §5.1 (bailout bullet: the offer states the shortfall and each option's
   coverage), and the in-game help content where the bailout is described.
9. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Presentation-only change to the offer.** No new engine rules, no change to
  when an offer is raised, which option the AI accepts, or what happens on
  accept/decline. The only state change is one extra field on the pending offer.
- **Snapshot, not recomputation.** The deficit must be captured when the offer is
  raised (`state.pendingLoanOffer`), because on the deferred-mutation path the
  turn's deltas are still un-applied when the dialog renders; recomputing from
  the live wallet in the model would show a wrong (post-pause) figure for a
  competitive seat or a deferred single-player closing.
- **Integer economy, integer copy.** Coins are integers (CG-0MTIO1M15001E9Y6); the
  figure is rounded/floored to a whole coin and never rendered as a fraction.
- **Overlay conventions.** Any new text uses the existing overlay patterns in
  `MainStreetLoanOverlay.ts` (depths 199/200/201, elements parented into
  `hudContainer`, pushed into `s.overlayObjects`, instant appearance), and the
  dialog content is produced by the Phaser-free
  `buildLoanOfferModel()` so it stays unit-testable.
- **No scope creep into the Turn Summary item.** The mid-game selector in
  MS-0MVPWSQMG004198C is in flight; this item must not modify it or block on it.

## Existing state

- The dialog copy is hard-coded in `buildLoanOfferModel()`
  (`src/scenes/MainStreetLoanOverlayModel.ts:153-156`): `intro` is
  `"You cannot cover this turn's costs.
Take a bank loan to keep playing, or
  decline to end the run."` and there is no amount anywhere in the model.
- `PendingLoanOffer` (`src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts:717`) carries only
  `ownerId`, `reason` and `options` — the deficit is discarded.
- The deficit **is** known at raise time: `maybeOfferBailoutForSeat()`
  (`src/MainStreetLoans.ts:335`) computes `coins` (from `opts.projectedCoins`,
  the competitive seat's `coins`, or `state.resourceBank.coins`) and only proceeds
  when `coins < 0`. Its log row already prints that number
  (`"... coins are -80; a bank loan is available ..."`).
- Callers pass the projected balance where it matters:
  `MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts:790` (`state.resourceBank.coins +
  pendingCoinDelta`), and `:1383` per competitive seat.
- The overlay (`src/scenes/MainStreetLoanOverlay.ts`) already renders a
  multi-line `intro` (with `lineSpacing`) and sizes its panel from
  `PANEL_CHROME_HEIGHT + rowCount * ROW_HEIGHT` — an extra warning line fits the
  layout without a redesign (chrome height may need one constant bump).
- Serialisation copies the offer field-by-field
  (`src/MainStreetStateSerialize.ts:158`) and `restorePendingLoanOffer()`
  (`src/MainStreetLoans.ts:694`) validates defensively, dropping the offer on
  malformed input — an added optional field must follow that same
  default-don't-drop pattern.
- Existing coverage: `tests/main-street/MainStreetLoanOverlay.test.ts` (model +
  deferred-closing flow), `MainStreetLoanOverlay.browser.test.ts` (asserts the
  current copy at line 106 — will need updating), `MainStreetLoanBailout.test.ts`,
  `MainStreetLoanCompetitive.test.ts`, `MainStreetLoanSaveLoad.test.ts`,
  `loan-headless-baseline.test.ts` (loans-off golden baseline).

## Desired change

1. **Carry the shortfall on the offer.**
   `PendingLoanOffer.shortfall: number` — the coins needed to reach zero at the
   closing, set in `maybeOfferBailoutForSeat()` from the very `coins` value used
   for the `coins < 0` test (`Math.max(0, -coins)`), so the dialog and the
   bankruptcy decision can never disagree.
2. **Serialise and restore it.** Include `shortfall` in the serialised
   `pendingLoanOffer` and validate it in `restorePendingLoanOffer()`: a finite
   non-negative integer is kept; a missing or malformed value restores as
   "unknown" (`null`/absent) and the dialog omits the figure instead of showing a
   wrong one. No schema version bump.
3. **Model the copy.** Extend `LoanOfferModel` with the shortfall figure / intro
   line, a per-row coverage flag plus the coins each row would still be short,
   and an optional `warning` line used when no presented option closes the gap.
   Rows keep their existing self-contained label and gain the coverage suffix.
4. **Render it.** Draw the amount line and (when present) the warning in
   `showLoanOfferDialog()`, growing the panel chrome height so the extra line
   does not collide with the option rows.
5. **Log consistently.** Update the bailout activity-log row to state the
   shortfall in coins rather than a raw negative balance.
6. **Document it.** `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` §5.1 bailout bullets
   plus `src/MainStreetHelpContent.ts` bank-loan/bailout help text.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts` — `PendingLoanOffer.shortfall` (optional/`number`),
  documented as a snapshot taken when the offer is raised.
- `src/MainStreetLoans.ts` — `maybeOfferBailoutForSeat()` records
  `Math.max(0, -coins)`; `restorePendingLoanOffer()` validates the new field;
  bailout log row copy.
- `src/MainStreetStateSerialize.ts` — serialise `shortfall` inside the
  `pendingLoanOffer` block (`:158`).
- `src/scenes/MainStreetLoanOverlayModel.ts` — `shortfall`, per-row
  `coversShortfall`/`stillShort`, `warning`, and the new `intro` copy.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetLoanOverlay.ts` — render the amount line and warning;
  bump `PANEL_CHROME_HEIGHT` if needed.
- `tests/main-street/MainStreetLoanOverlay.test.ts` — model text, row coverage,
  no-option-covers warning, unknown-shortfall fallback.
- `tests/main-street/MainStreetLoanBailout.test.ts` — shortfall recorded from the
  real engine paths (single-player + deferred projected balance).
- `tests/main-street/MainStreetLoanCompetitive.test.ts` — per-seat shortfall from
  `PlayerRecord.coins`.
- `tests/main-street/MainStreetLoanSaveLoad.test.ts` — round-trip plus
  pre-field (v3 without `shortfall`) save.
- `tests/main-street/MainStreetLoanOverlay.browser.test.ts` — rendered amount and
  warning text (replaces the `"You cannot cover this turn's costs"` assertion).
- `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` — §5.1 bailout bullets.

  here should touch it or wait on it.

  turn's expected income/costs, a safety buffer, or "you can survive N turns").
- Changing the loan menu, interest, repayment timing, AI policy or when an offer
  is raised — including "always offer a loan big enough to cover the shortfall"
  (a real option the producer explicitly did not choose; see Risks).
- Any audio/animation work for the dialog; the overlay stays instant and
  reduced-motion safe.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption — deficit, not a projection.** "How much is needed to get to the
  next turn" is read as the exact shortfall at the closing decision point
  (`max(0, −coins)`), which is what the loan must restore to zero for play to
  continue. A forward-looking buffer was considered and is listed as a non-goal.
- **Risk — biggest option may not be enough.** With the default menu the largest
  option is €1000; a deeper shortfall (a large incident plus repayments) means no
  option rescues the seat, and today the dialog gives no hint. Mitigation: AC3's
  per-row coverage and the no-option-covers warning; a test pins that warning.
- **Risk — stale figure after a resume.** If the shortfall were recomputed at
  render time, a resumed/deferred closing could show a different number from the
  one that raised the offer. Mitigation: snapshot on the offer (AC2), with a
  deferred-path test.
- **Risk — save compatibility.** An additive field inside `pendingLoanOffer` still
  touches the restore validator; a strict validator could drop a whole offer and
  strand the closing. Mitigation: default-don't-drop restore rules plus a test
  for a save without the field.
- **Risk — copy churn.** Several existing assertions embed the current intro
  string (browser test line 106) and the log phrasing; leaving them untouched
  would silently pass. Mitigation: AC3/AC4 keep the dialog and the log in step and
  the listed tests are updated in the same change.
- **Risk — scope creep.** Natural "while we're here" additions (the Turn Summary
  selector, forward projections, a bigger bailout menu, a HUD shortfall readout)
  are recorded as non-goals/related work rather than absorbed.
- **Assumption — no new HUD element.** The amount belongs to the dialog only; the
  HUD keeps showing the coin balance and the existing loan obligation readout.

  (completed). Built `MainStreetLoanOverlay.ts` / `MainStreetLoanOverlayModel.ts`
  and the deferred-closing resume this item extends; its overlay conventions are
  reused unchanged.
- **MS-0MVPWS9L9001PVXG — Bailout offer, AI policy and headless resolution**
  (completed). Owns `maybeOfferBailout`/`maybeOfferBailoutForSeat` — the functions
  that gain the `shortfall` snapshot.
- **MS-0MVPWSAMH005LV9R — Competitive seat bailout parity** (completed). Per-seat
  offers read `PlayerRecord.coins`; the shortfall must follow that same balance.
- **MS-0MVPWSE0E003QLKE — Persistence: loans and pending offer (v3)** (completed).
  The serialisation/restore path the new field extends, and the reason no schema
  bump is needed.
- **MS-0MVPWSFDN000QJXB — Documentation and in-game help for loans** (completed).
  Owns the §5.1 bailout prose and the help panel copy updated here.
- **MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG — Bank Loans** (completed epic). Parent feature; this is a
  presentation refinement of its bailout flow.
- **MS-0MVPWSQMG004198C — Wire Bank Loan button into Turn Summary dialog**
  (open, `plan_complete`) — with children MS-0MVXYCHCJ002ER7L (test-first loans
  descriptor/selector model), MS-0MVXYCIU00053HL1 (loan eligibility in the
  deferred-closing window) and MS-0MVXYCKFE000VF76 (confirm dispatches
  `takeLoan`, blocked). **Related, not blocking and not dependent**: that item
  covers mid-game borrowing; if the producer wants the same shortfall wording
  there, it should be raised on that item, not absorbed here.
- Duplicate check performed — `wl search "shortfall"` and `wl search "loan offer"`
  show no item that surfaces the bailout deficit in the dialog; the closest items
  use "shortfall" only for repayment/unclamped-repayment semantics. No duplicate.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

No interview round was run: the seed ("On the bank loan offer explain how much is
needed to get to the next turn") plus the repo identifies the target — the dialog
titled *Bank Loan Offer*
(`src/scenes/MainStreetLoanOverlayModel.ts`, `title: 'Bank Loan Offer'`) — and the
mechanic fixes the figure (the closing deficit that raised the offer). Choices
that were not answerable from the seed are recorded below as explicit,
non-blocking assumptions for producer confirmation.

- **Q: Which surface should show the amount?**
  — Decision (agent, from the seed): the **bankruptcy bailout dialog** only
  ("the bank loan offer" is that dialog's title). Source: seed wording +
  `buildLoanOfferModel()` title string. Related, out of scope:
  MS-0MVPWSQMG004198C's mid-game selector.
- **Q: What exactly is "needed to get to the next turn"?**
  — Decision (agent): the closing shortfall `max(0, −coins)` — the coins required
  to restore a non-negative balance so the seat continues into the next turn.
  Source: `maybeOfferBailoutForSeat()` only raises an offer when `coins < 0`, and

- **Q: Show only the amount, or also whether each option covers it?**

the renderer publishes per-seat anchors: one live anchor per rendered row,
